limitations: The prior candidate.4 review was processed only as opaque bytes for mandatory size/SHA-256 validation; its semantic content was not read.

The raw candidate.2 tar.gz container is not present. The materialized 201-member tree, receipt, control files, member ledger, and replay transcript were independently checked, but the tar.gz container hash and tar metadata could not be recomputed directly.

No fresh virtual environment, wheel build, pytest, or Ruff process was executed because the bundle is read-only. The retained rebuilt wheel was compared byte-for-byte with the frozen wheel, its RECORD was verified, and all 61 packaged Python files were compared with current-source/runtime/src.

Exact semantics for DG10-C4-AI-013 through DG10-C4-AI-018 are not materialized outside the semantically prohibited prior candidate.4 review. The identity-supersession report supplies only IDs and unmapped reason codes.

findings.rationale: The release decision is recomputed, but from artifacts that remain locally mintable. controlled_decision accepts generic R3-R8 and L1-L5 stage receipts through _verify_stage_receipt, which checks outer fields and hashes but no fixed stage-specific importer or underlying verdict semantics. Machine-gate, independent-replay, and claim-validation receipts likewise validate generic PASS envelopes and evidence references. authorize_release therefore reproduces a decision from caller-selected, hand-constructible receipts and can return release_authorized=true without authentic stage issuers.
findings.required_action: Require fixed, stage-specific importer outputs; replay each underlying raw gate result and AI provenance; bind every receipt to the fixed active identity set; and prohibit generic stage, machine-gate, replay, or claim-validation envelopes from authorizing release.
findings.title: Release authorization still trusts generic locally mintable PASS receipts

findings.rationale: The importer recomputes an offered bundle, but does not require the fixed candidate.4 review-bundle receipt/digest or prove that its current-source closure equals the separately selected identity receipt. Its CLI accepts arbitrary bundle, bundle-receipt, and identity-receipt paths. Authorization also accepts any internally consistent local identity receipt and any nonempty subset source inventory; it does not require the active candidate.4.3 identity path or the frozen 788a5ec4... source root. Two audits can therefore review a substitute incomplete bundle and receive stage receipts bound to a different caller-selected identity set.
findings.required_action: Pin the exact bundle receipt path, manifest hash, c9c03df8... bundle root, active identity receipt path, 788a5ec4... source root, environment identity, and model identity. Require exact equality between bundle current-source entries and the active source inventory before minting or consuming receipts.
findings.title: Bootstrap import and authorization permit bundle and identity substitution

findings.rationale: The content-addressed Runtime wheel, rebuild equality, fresh-install capture, and 204-test/Ruff captures are present and internally consistent. However, runner_and_helper_closure contains 327 entries and omits files executed or loaded by the captured pytest run, including tests/conftest.py, tests/test_package_dg10_results.py, tests/test_release_safety.py, and contract/config inputs. The BFCL binding is only an author-reported Git HEAD plus dirty=false, without a materialized tree/member manifest or command capture. Consequently the captured execution is not independently bound to its complete imported test/config and upstream byte closure.
findings.required_action: Bind the capture to the full collected-test, conftest, contract/config, runner, helper, and imported-file set; include a safe upstream BFCL tree/member manifest and dirty-state capture; then rerun the rebuild, fresh install, full pytest, and Ruff capture against that exact closure.
findings.title: R2 execution capture is not bound to the complete executed source/config closure

findings.rationale: The preflight now consumes the importer aggregate and derives 24 slot IDs, but no bundled execution path constructs AttemptLedger with authorization.authorized_bootstrap_slots before provider access. authorized_model_call_slots remains optional, and authorized_bootstrap_slots is consumed by the post-hoc T2 gate rather than an actual call boundary. The ledger also has no latch implementing the policy requirement that any failure or identity drift deny all remaining slots.
findings.required_action: Provide one target-model executor that revalidates the fixed authorization receipt before every call, constructs the ledger with exactly the authorized slots, journals each slot before provider access, atomically prevents reuse, and permanently denies remaining slots after any failure or identity drift.
findings.title: Exact 24-call authorization is not wired to the model-call boundary

findings.rationale: The quality gate now enforces two disjoint 50-case strata and artifact references, but the AI test-access importer only requires numeric open_p0_count/open_p1_count values of zero and that findings is a list; it does not validate finding entries or recompute counts from OPEN severities. It also accepts any self-consistent offered review bundle, and the resulting APPROVE_ONE_FULL_TEST receipt has no atomic one-use consumption mechanism. Inconsistent findings or repeated full-test execution can therefore pass the approval path.
findings.required_action: Pin the test-access review bundle and schema, validate every finding and recompute open counts, bind the audit to the exact active identities and quality artifacts, and issue an atomically consumed one-shot full-test capability.
findings.title: AI test-access approval can ignore open findings and is not one-shot

findings.rationale: The scorer now derives categories from a 216-case manifest and enforces 80/122/24 denominators and dependency hashes. The supplied manifest itself has no frozen_at, parent-contract binding, fixed path/digest, or proof that it predates result access. A caller can still create or reclassify a denominator-correct manifest after seeing results.
findings.required_action: Pre-register the exact BFCL manifest path and digest before any case execution or result access, bind its timestamp and acceptance contract, and require all generation, scoring, ledger, and gate consumers to use that fixed digest.
findings.title: BFCL categories are derived but the case manifest is not preregistration-bound

findings.rationale: ServingAttempt validation and summarize_cell enforce useful per-attempt invariants, but build_serving_gate still accepts caller-created cell mappings. It does not reconstruct cells from the reconciled ledger or raw attempt/resource/trace receipts, and cross-cell ledger/model hashes are compared only as supplied values. Fabricated internally consistent cell summaries can therefore pass.
findings.required_action: Build every cell inside the gate from a globally reconciled ledger and verified raw receipts; bind the fixed workload, source, environment, model, and ledger identities; and reject caller-authored summary mappings.
findings.title: Serving acceptance still trusts caller-authored cell summaries

findings.rationale: The frozen claim matrix records R0-R2 as REVIEW_REQUIRED, while stage-specific reports record AUTHOR_CANDIDATE and a later importer can create ACCEPTED receipts. There is still no common append-only stage ledger or explicit supersession record consumed by every report, claim validator, authorization gate, and release gate. Consumers select different snapshots rather than reconciling one current state.
findings.required_action: Introduce one append-only candidate-bound stage ledger with receipt hashes and explicit supersession events, and require every report, validator, authorization path, and release path to resolve the same current state.
findings.title: Candidate.4 still lacks one reconciled append-only stage state

findings.required_action: Materialize the exact DG10-C4-AI-013 semantics in a separate immutable successor finding register that is permitted for blind review, then re-audit the cited bytes.
findings.title: DG10-C4-AI-013 cannot be semantically re-evaluated from permitted evidence

DG10-R0.rationale: The 201 materialized members, control files, receipt, replay ledger, immutable candidate.2 NO-GO, and candidate.3 succession evidence replay cleanly. R0 nevertheless remains open because the candidate.4 parent finding semantics are not materialized under the required blind boundary and the importer can bind acceptance to substitute bundle and identity roots.

DG10-R1.rationale: The xhigh AI policy is truthful, claim validation and the append-only ledger core are materially improved, and current contracts deny model, test, and release access. Blocking bypasses remain in bundle/identity selection, pre-call 24-slot enforcement, test-access approval, and generic release receipts; BFCL, serving, and stage-state P2 gaps also remain.

DG10-R2.rationale: The 372-entry source inventory is exact; the frozen and rebuilt wheels are byte-identical; wheel RECORD and all packaged Python files match source; and the retained fresh-install, 204-pytest, and Ruff captures hash correctly. R2 is not semantically closed because the capture's 327-entry execution closure omits executed test/config inputs, upstream BFCL is not independently tree-replayed, active identities are substitutable at authorization, and the C4 parent findings lack permitted semantics.
